name: boot
titel: In a Wooden Boat at Sea

gruppen.name: see_fern
gruppen.text: Surf and swell far out, all around the horizon. It reaches you over the gunwale and is softened by it.

gruppen.name: wind
gruppen.text: A light wind from ahead – the boat lies at anchor with its bow into the wind. It slowly rises and falls; in the gusts it freshens – the same gusts that fill the sail.

gruppen.name: wellen
gruppen.text: Wave crests 7 to 32 m away, rolling in from ahead with the wind in long lines that stretch from left to right – each crest is several metres wide, and its sound comes from along the whole front. When one breaks with real force, there is a deep rumble.

gruppen.name: rumpf
gruppen.text: Slaps and splashes against the planks – on whichever side is dipping as the boat rolls. The wood resonates hollowly and carries every knock right to your ear; hard hits make the whole hull boom, and now and then a little spray flies over the gunwale and patters onto the wood beside you.

gruppen.name: knarzen
gruppen.text: Rowlocks, thwarts and frames work as the boat heels or a wave hits the hull: a calm, warm creaking that stays fixed to the boat – only the deep, woody creaks, no bright squeaks.

gruppen.name: segel
gruppen.text: The sail hangs slack on the mast in front of you, beyond your feet. In a gust it catches the wind: real cloth flutter swells, the canvas fills with a soft thump and collapses again.

gruppen.name: moewen_fern
gruppen.text: The distant chatter of the colony, from the same direction.

gruppen.name: moewen
gruppen.text: Five gulls keep to windward, ahead of you, circling there in the wind and calling; now and then another answers. When the wind freshens or a wave breaks on the rock, they take fright.

gruppen.name: ueberflug
gruppen.text: About every half minute a gull shoots over the boat 3 to 5 m up – mostly across your view along the coast, from right to left, sometimes the other way, and once in a while one comes in diagonally, from ahead or from behind. One call lands right overhead, its pitch dropping as it passes (Doppler); wingbeats as it approaches.

gruppen.name: moewen_weit
gruppen.text: A gull colony on a distant rock ahead and to the right, 150 to 370 metres away – its calls always come from that direction.

gruppen.name: felsen
gruppen.text: A rock juts out of the water about 20 m away. Now and then a wave slams into it – a hard impact, then the spray falls back. The boat slowly swings, so the rock wanders around you.

gruppen.name: zug
gruppen.text: Twice in ten minutes a flock of eight to twelve gulls flies along the coast in front of you, 45 to 75 m away – from right to left, later back from left to right. For half a minute you hear it come, pass calling and fade; its chatter comes from several places across the flock.

gruppen.name: gaense
gruppen.text: Twice a skein of geese flies along the coast in front of you, high and 60 to 100 m away – first from right to left, later back. Their calls carry for a long time and come from all along the skein.

gruppen.name: schwebung
gruppen.text: The gentle E–G harmony that used to hide in one of the sea recordings, transcribed and played as a soft, dark, slowly changing pad with a binaural beat: every tone in your right ear sits exactly 8 Hz above the one in your left ear. The gentle 8 Hz pulse you perceive is created by your brain from that difference – at the border between theta and alpha, relaxed but not sleepy. Works only with headphones.

text: You lie in an open wooden sailing boat at anchor, a good six metres long – at the stern on cushions, your head propped up against the aft thwart, feet towards the bow, which points into the wind. Gulls circle ahead and fly along the coast in front of you, waves roll in from ahead in long lines, water knocks hollow against the planks, the boat creaks and swings slowly on its anchor, and now and then the wind catches the slack sail.
Calm sea; the gulls circle at ease.
A skein of geese crosses in front of you; you can hear their calls for a long time.
A flock of gulls flies past along the coast as the wind rises.
The wind freshens; the sail fills more often.
The waves grow, the hull is hit harder; the gulls call more excitedly, their cries blown about by the wind.
Heavy sea: breakers crash against the rock one after another.
The wind drops and the sea settles.
Calm again – the gulls circle lazily once more.
